name: Continue to Stormwind
summary: You carry a requisition from Sentinel Hill to Stormwind by gryphon, where Osric Strang awaits in Old Town.

sections.title: Taking Wing
sections.body: Quartermaster Lewis prepares a requisition note at Sentinel Hill. Thor, the local gryphon master, offers you the fastest way out of the contested plains. For a modest fee, you ride one of the kingdom’s trained gryphons above dusty farmlands and Elwynn Forest’s river border. Then the gryphon carries you over Stormwind City’s high white ramparts.

sections.title: Old Town Supply Lines
sections.body: You land at the capital’s trade roosts, then make your way into Old Town. There you find Osric Strang at his shop, Limited Immunity. Osric supplies the frontier, yet his grim reception shows the growing rift between Westfall’s beleaguered People’s Militia and the distracted rulers in Stormwind Keep.

faq.q: What is the purpose of this quest?
faq.answer: You carry Quartermaster Lewis’s requisition from Sentinel Hill to Stormwind by gryphon. Along the way, you learn the route between the outpost and the capital.
Osric Strang runs Limited Immunity in Old Town, inside Stormwind City.

faq.q: Why does Sentinel Hill need supplies from Stormwind?
faq.answer: The People’s Militia at Sentinel Hill struggles against the Defias Brotherhood and receives little formal military aid from the capital. Quartermaster Lewis must buy gear directly from civilian merchants.
Thor is the gryphon master at Sentinel Hill. He manages routes connecting Westfall to Stormwind City and other friendly hubs.
Lewis’s Note is an urgent requisition from Quartermaster Lewis, listing the gear and provisions needed to keep Sentinel Hill’s garrison equipped.

faq.q: What happens after delivering the note?
faq.answer: After Osric receives the requisition, he sends you to speak with Stormwind’s gryphon master, Dungar Longdrink. You arrange transport of the ordered supplies back to Westfall.

angles.text: As an Alliance traveler, you can rely on gryphon masters to connect scattered outposts and keep remote garrisons linked to the capital.
As a human, you can see in Old Town how distant common citizens and isolated frontiersmen feel from the politics of the grand House of Nobles.
